Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has myopia, which means she has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly. We've noticed this since she started school and are exploring options for corrective lenses.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She tends to turn the volume of the TV up quite high to hear her favorite shows comfortably. This could indicate a potential issue with her hearing that we're keeping an eye on.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Lately, she's complained about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods like ice cream or frozen yogurt. It's become a concern for us as parents because she loves these treats but winces in pain after consuming them.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our pediatrician recommended regular heart check-ups due to a familial history of cardiac issues. These check-ups help monitor her heart health closely and catch any potential problems early.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, she experiences hypotonia‚ which affects her muscle tone. This condition makes her muscles feel stiffer than they should be‚ and we're working with therapists to manage its impact on her daily life.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: She has constipation issues‚ which can be frustrating at times. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues somewhat‚ but it's an ongoing challenge.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: In addition to her specific health concerns‚ she takes longer to reach certain developmental milestones than her peers‚ and there are some palatal abnormalities we're monitoring closely with her healthcare team. These aspects require consistent attention and adaptation to ensure she receives the support she needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a familial history of cardiac issues and undergoes regular heart check-ups to monitor her heart health closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with 38% having heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be managed through diet and hydration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and constipation can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone, and is working with therapists to manage its impact on her daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurological issues, including seizures, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with around 20-40% experiencing seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up quite high to hear her favorite shows comfortably, indicating a potential issue with her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hearing loss and recurrent otitis media or glue ear can cause conductive hearing loss in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly, and is exploring options for corrective lenses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, which is a concern for her parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth, can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach certain developmental milestones than her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach certain developmental milestones than her peers, and has some palatal abnormalities that require consistent attention and adaptation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and hip dysplasia, can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing health
* Eyesight review to monitor vision health
* Cardiac review to monitor heart health
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of constipation issues and adaptation of diet and hydration to manage symptoms

* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe. Around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have inconsistent hearing, sometimes responding well to sounds and other times not, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient reports blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental problems requiring constant check-ups and treatments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and possibly other behavioral differences, though specifics are not detailed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head. * Hearing reviews to age 5 to address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct any vision problems.

* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past, which is an infection of the middle ear, and has required treatment.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular cardiac check-ups due to a potential heart condition, although currently, there's nothing to worry about.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and has certain foods she refuses to eat, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, which means her muscles are a bit too stiff at times, and she does exercises at home to help loosen them up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the volume up really high on the TV or her toys, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a habit of sitting way too close to the television or when reading books, suggesting potential eyesight problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to other kids her age, which affects her speech a little bit.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking, which may be related to her hypotonia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for any skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address any challenges
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has astigmatism, which affects her vision. She sees things slightly blurred at times and has trouble focusing on close objects. We've had her glasses prescribed to help correct this.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There seems to be an issue with her hearing; she can pick up some sounds without difficulty, but struggles with others. It's as if she's not registering certain frequencies or volumes. This has been noticeable in both quiet and noisy environments.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her front teeth are noticeably larger than those of her peers. This has been a concern for us, especially in terms of aesthetics and potential orthodontic interventions down the line.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She tires easily during physical activities. Even simple tasks like running around in the playground or climbing stairs leave her breathless and needing rest. This limitation on physical endurance is concerning and impacts her ability to participate fully in school sports and play.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She gets exhausted quickly when engaging in physical activities. This isn't just about cardiovascular endurance; it seems there's a neurologicall component where her brain and muscles don't seem to coordinate as efficiently as they should.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Bowel movements have been irregular. There are times when she experiences constipation, and at others, she has diarrhea. Managing her diet has become essential to try and regulate these issues.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Despite being 8 years old, her speech development is delayed. She doesn't articulate as many words or express herself as clearly as children of the same age. This has been another significant concern for us.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily during physical activities, which suggests potential cardiac issues affecting endurance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, with episodes of constipation and diarrhea, requiring dietary management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues can be present, with some individuals requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits neurological issues, including easy exhaustion during physical activities, suggesting a neurologic component affecting coordination and endurance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Seizures are reported in approximately 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome, and can be of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, struggling with certain frequencies or volumes, indicating potential conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision, causing blurry vision and trouble focusing on close objects, corrected with glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are common, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, which may require orthodontic interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns are common, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech development, not articulating as many words or expressing herself as clearly as children of the same age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, are common.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal issues, including short fingers, curvature of the 5th fingers, and hip dysplasia, can be present, with some individuals requiring medical review and potential interventions.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac function.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to evaluate skeletal development.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental and functional needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in his heart, which is a source of concern and requires regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement irregularities and discomfort, which are being addressed through diet and lifestyle changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had seizures, which are a source of concern and are being managed with the help of a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often not responding immediately to his name being called, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, squints, and has difficulty seeing clearly, which are concerns that need to be addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods and drinks, and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not speaking as much as expected for his age, which is a concern that needs to be addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school but may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness.
* Regular hearing reviews to address conductive hearing loss and potential speech delay.
* Eyesight review to correct blurry vision and squinting.
* Cardiac review to monitor the valve issue in the heart.
* Neurological management to control seizures.
* Speech therapy to address speech delay and communication difficulties.
* Consideration of occupational therapy and physiotherapy to support development and motor skills.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue identified at birth, requiring regular check-ups and management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to struggle with hearing certain sounds, despite normal hearing tests.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs his eyes when trying to focus, especially during screen time or reading, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

Parent: Honestly, I'm not entirely sure, but she does seem to squint a lot when looking at things far away. It's like her eyes aren't focusing right or something.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had glue ear last year and needed antibiotics. It was a real challenge getting her to take the medicine but thankfully it cleared up okay.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing can be tough for her. Harder foods like apples or meat are tricky - she tends to avoid them because it hurts her teeth or jaws.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: I've noticed she gets really tired easily. When playing with friends or running around, she can't keep going for as long as they do. Maybe it's just because she's not used to it yet?

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Sometimes she trips over her own feet or bumps into furniture. Her coordination isn't like other kids her age - it's almost like she's still learning how to move properly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feedings been a battle since day one. She has this aversion to certain textures or smells - it makes meal times really stressful.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Generally, she moves a bit... differently. Not like the other kids. Hard to describe but maybe it's related to the coordination thing?

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired easily, particularly when engaging in physical activities like playing or running, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, showing aversion to certain textures or smells, making meal times stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes trips over her own feet or bumps into furniture, indicating coordination issues, and has been described as moving differently.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and there are reports of neurological developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, which was treated with antibiotics, and tends to squint when looking at things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to squint when looking at things far away, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with chewing, especially with harder foods, and avoids them due to discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and moves differently than other children.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curvature of the 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect and manage hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and coordination issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about her eyesight. She sits way too close to the television and books, and I'm afraid it's going to affect her vision in the long run. I've tried to limit her screen time, but it's hard when she gets so engrossed in cartoons.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... she seems to have trouble hearing certain sounds. Like, sometimes I'll call her name and she won't respond until I say it louder or get her attention another way. It's like she hears some things but not others clearly.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Well... eating can be a challenge for her. Harder foods like meats or crunchy vegetables are difficult for her to chew. We've had to adjust our meal times to make sure she can manage her food safely.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist found a valve issue in her heart. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it closely. I get anxious about her playing too vigorously or getting overly tired because of this condition.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately... she falls more often than the other kids her age. Her balance seems off sometimes. We're working on making her environment safer to prevent injuries.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Yes... bowel movements have been a concern. Constipation has been an issue at times. We try to keep her diet balanced to help regulate these problems.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Actually... yes. There are two main concerns. First, she has a speech delay; her language skills aren't developing as quickly as they should. Second, she was diagnosed with hip dysplasia. We're seeing specialists for both conditions and following their advice closely to ensure she receives the right care and support.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular monitoring and check-ups with a cardiologist to ensure stability and control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight at a slower rate compared to her peers, which is being discussed with her pediatrician to rule out any underlying issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and slow weight gain are common in children with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding and others having long-lasting lack of interest in feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy, which is being managed by her neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, although some cases can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing, particularly when called from a distance, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty seeing the board clearly during lessons and squints or leans forward to get a better view, suggesting vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and prefers softer options, indicating some discomfort or difficulty with her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech delay, which is being addressed through regular speech therapy sessions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many requiring Educational Health Care Plans or special schooling, and some having more significant learning difficulties.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's posture appears noticeably different when standing or walking, which is being explored with her physical therapist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD, and may require physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's posture appears noticeably different when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, with some requiring monitoring or treatment.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental and behavioural concerns
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring and management of epilepsy and other neurological conditions

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about food and often refuses certain types, which can be frustrating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the TV volume way up to hear properly, indicating potential hearing concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which can make reading and writing a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

Parent: N/A.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in her heart, similar to what some other children have, requiring regular check-ups with the cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which has been an issue since she was little, and has been managed with different diets and exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes has brief blank spells where she just stares off into space, which are brief but worrisome, and efforts are being made to figure out what causes them and how to help her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media when she was younger, which is an ear infection, and monitoring of her hearing is ongoing to ensure it doesn't come back.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up, and glasses have helped a lot, but it's still something being kept an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, and short- or long sightedness, and squint can occasionally be a feature.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's front teeth are larger than average, which can make biting and chewing a bit more difficult, and care for them is being managed with a dentist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which affects the socket of her hip joint, and palatal abnormalities, which are being monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not affected by the otitis media.
* Ongoing monitoring of the patient's vision to adjust glasses as necessary.
* Regular check-ups with the cardiologist to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Management and treatment of the patient's constipation through diet and exercise.
* Investigation into the causes of the patient's blank spells and appropriate treatment.
* Monitoring of the patient's hip dysplasia and palatal abnormalities.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences exhaustion quickly during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky and refuses certain foods, making mealtime a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and turns the TV volume up really high, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has trouble seeing things clearly, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences sensitivity and discomfort in her teeth when eating cold foods or drinking cold water.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not speak as much as expected for her age, and the parent worries about potential underlying issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to evaluate and correct vision problems
* Cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year and needed antibiotics.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, and is working on correcting it with glasses and exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's front teeth are larger than usual, which sometimes makes eating and speaking a little tricky.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was diagnosed with hip dysplasia, and is following up with the orthopedic specialist regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor bone age and skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and coordination

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties with mealtime, being picky, and having trouble finishing meals, which raises concerns about his nutrition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly during physical activity and has difficulty making himself understood when speaking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing and turns the volume of the TV very high, suggesting hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, often squints, and has trouble reading unless it's very large.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when speaking and gets tired quickly during physical activity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to address hearing difficulties
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Referral for a skeletal review to assess spinal structure and undescended testes
* Consideration of speech therapy to address communication difficulties
* Occupational therapy to help with mealtime and feeding difficulties
* Physiotherapy to improve physical activity endurance
